claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-013 was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk that left the vendor unapproved within the documented diligence window, even though no confirmed control failure was formally logged.
specific_concerns: Evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, so the cited records cannot be independently checked for wording, scope, or materiality.
The policy requires a material unresolved risk for rejection; the summary shows quality-process gaps and a questionnaire inconsistency, but materiality is asserted more than demonstrated.
The packet correctly avoids claiming a proven control failure, but it still moves from follow-up-worthy issues to rejection without a clearly evidenced decision rule or threshold.
The summary references unmet approval follow-up, but does not show the formal approval status, owner, deadline, or whether rejection rather than hold/escalation was the required disposition.
unsupported_claims: That the unresolved issues were definitively material enough to require rejection rather than further follow-up or escalation.
That the vendor remained unsuitable for award as a policy-required outcome, rather than a conservative discretionary choice, based on the admissible record alone.
That the cited evidence establishes the exact approval predicate failure, rather than only documenting unresolved diligence questions.
evidence_requests: Provide the text or extract of BPROC-013-B showing the quality-process gap and whether it was tied to approval criteria.
Provide the text or extract of BPROC-013-C and BPROC-013-D showing the storage-control inconsistency and whether it remained unresolved at decision time.
Provide the text or extract of BPROC-013-E showing the procurement recommendation, including whether unresolved storage controls blocked approval or merely required follow-up.
Provide the governing procurement approval criterion or decision record showing when unresolved diligence issues become reject-level material risk rather than a hold or escalation.
decision_criteria: Rejection is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies alone justify follow-up or escalation, not proof of a reject-level control failure.
No private or unlogged security-review result may be cited or indirectly relied on.
Because only the Actor's summary is available, independent support is limited to whether the conclusion is plausibly framed within policy, not fully verified.
